before: Georgia law under O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120 et seq. classifies side-by-side vehicles alongside ATVs for regulatory purposes, restricting their use on public roads and establishing age and safety requirements. South Carolina regulates off-highway vehicles under S.C. Code § 56-15-10 et seq., with similar restrictions on road use and requirements for equipment standards.
after: Georgia treats side-by-sides, like ATVs, as off-road vehicles under O.C.G.A. § 40-7-1 et seq., and its law does not generally authorize them on public roads. South Carolina bars unregistered off-road vehicles from highways (S.C. Code § 56-3-110); registered UTVs may use some roads from Nov. 18, 2026 (Act 164).

before: Generally no. Georgia (O.C.G.A. § 40-7-120) and South Carolina (S.C. Code § 56-15-10) restrict side-by-side operation on public roads, with limited exceptions. Operating illegally on a road can affect liability determinations in an accident case.
after: Generally no. Georgia does not generally allow it; South Carolina allows only registered UTVs on certain roads, starting Nov. 18, 2026 (S.C. Act 164 of 2026). Operating illegally on a road can affect liability determinations in an accident case.
